the tissue distribution and developmental changes of Aldh mRNA expression were determined and the regulation of Aldh mRNAs by MEIs was studied.

the mRNA expression of 15 Aldhs in adult mouse tissues is organ- and sex-specific, and the mRNA expression of most Aldhs in adult liver is induced by typical microsomal MEIs, except for the PXR ligands and AhR ligands, which induce Aldh1a and 3a mRNA expression, respectively.

the mRNA expression of 15 aldehyde dehydrogeases (Aldh enzymes) is differentially regulated in mice tissues and that the expression of Aldh mRNAs is generally insensitive to typical phase-I microsomal inducer except PPAR alpha activators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tissue distribution and developmental regulation of Aldh enzymes and their regulation by typical MEIs in mice.
the tissue distribution, ontogenetic changes, and regulation of the mRNA of Aldh enzymes by typical microsomal MEIs.
the tissue distribution, developmental changes, and regulation of Aldh enzymes mRNA expression in mouse tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Aldhs are not regulated by MEI ligands except by the PPAR alpha ligand, fenofibrate.
the mRNA expression of all the Aldh enzymes is highly regulated by PPAR alpha activators, whereas the expression of Aldh enzymes by other MEIs is organ specific and enzyme specific.

, in contrast to CYP450 enzymes that have been extensively studied and characterized, the role of Aldh enzymes in xenobiotic metabolism, elimination, or organ-specific toxicity has not been fully elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of Aldh enzymes is regulated in a tissue-, developmental- and inducer-specific manner.
the tissue distribution and regulation of Aldhs by prototypical microsome inducers is complex and varies with different Aldh enzymes.
, in general, the expression of Aldh mRNA in adult mouse tissues is relatively low and is regulated by PPAR alpha ligand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Aldh expression is highly tissue-specific and that the expression of many Aldh enzymes is regulated by microsomal enzyme inducing agents.
the expression of Aldh enzymes is organ specific, gender specific, and inducible by PPAR alpha ligand.
Aldh enzymes are expressed at different levels in different tissues, and their regulation by MEIs is tissue-specific.
